tip: Indonesian rarely marks plurals, but para does it for people: para pekerja = the workers, as a group. It never goes on things.
One root ajar, two people: pengajar is the teacher (from mengajar, to teach), pelajar the student (from belajar, to study).
pe- also builds doers from nouns: kemudi is the steering wheel, so pengemudi is the driver – the person at the kemudi.
Compound nouns run head first: pemandu wisata is literally 'guide tourism' – the reverse of English 'tour guide'.
A few doer nouns take bare pe- with no sound change: tani gives petani (farmer), not penani – kerja gives pekerja the same way.
bangun means both 'wake up' and 'build'. bangunan comes from the second: a thing built, a building.
Before a verb, baru is not 'new' – it means 'only just / only then': baru datang setelah tiga puluh menit = only came after thirty minutes.
-an usually makes things, but kenalan is a person: someone you know. kenalan lama = an old acquaintance, not old knowledge.
oleh-oleh, souvenirs you bring back, is a fixed doubled word – don't read it as the preposition oleh (by) said twice.
per-…-an nouns pair with ber- verbs: bertemu (meet) gives pertemuan (a meeting), just as berjalan gives perjalanan.
To name an action, take the meN- verb and swap me- for pe-, then add -an: memeriksa (check) becomes pemeriksaan (a check).
penjualan is the selling, penjual the seller – one -an apart. Penjualan tiket konser = concert ticket sales, an activity, not a person.
ke-…-an also names events, and the verb stays whole inside: berangkat (depart) sits intact in keberangkatan (departure).
kehilangan takes its object directly: kehilangan dompet = losing the wallet – no word for 'of' in between.
Time gets eaten in Indonesian: memakan waktu satu jam = takes an hour, literally 'eats one hour'.
